title: Model error decision tree and UX hypotheses
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a working note that explores a focused UX for surfacing and helping engineers triage model-level failures (timeouts, 5xx from serving runtime, decode/model failures, and behavioral model errors). Goal: reduce mean time-to-diagnosis by guiding users down a principled decision tree and by making the most relevant artifacts (inputs, outputs, traces, resource metrics) accessible in one pane.

Problem statements we want the UI to address:
- Users currently receive opaque 5xx/timeouts without quick contextual signals. They open logs or re-run requests manually, which is slow.
- Model errors (e.g., null tokens, invalid JSON output) are buried in the text stream - hard to correlate with model version, prompt mold, or hardware flakiness.
- There is no lightweight way to test hypotheses (trim prompt, change max_tokens, swap quantized model) from the same failure view.

High-level product hypotheses:
H1: Presenting a "recommended next step" (rerun with trimmed prompt / swap to fallback model / requeue to slower lane) will surface the fastest path to resolution >50% of cases.
H2: An automatically generated "failure fingerprint" (classification + likely root cause candidates) reduces investigation time by 30% for SRE/engineers.
H3: Lightweight in-place replay and diff (input vs. sanitized input, token-level alignment) will reduce unnecessary ticket escalation.

Proposed view: "Failure Investigator" (single screen, three-column responsive layout)
- Left column: Failure summary + quick actions
  - Top: single-line summary: timestamp, route, model (vX.Y), outcome (timeout / 5xx / model-error) with colored pill.
  - Fingerprint card: auto-classified tags ("inference-timeout", "kv-cache-miss", "out_of_memory", "invalid-json", "truncated-output"). Each tag has a confidence score and the rule that matched (e.g. timeout > 12000ms).
  - Suggested first action (primary CTA): Rerun with prompt pruning OR Switch to fallback model OR Requeue to dedicated lane. Secondary: Create incident / Attach to runbook.
  - Quick stats: p50/p95 latency for this route in the last 1h, error rate spike % vs baseline.

- Middle column: Replay + I/O inspector (primary investigation surface)
  - Compact session replay timeline showing: request start, token-chunk emits, KV cache hits, server-side retries, final failure event. Hover shows timestamps and raw logs.
  - Input pane (collapsible): original prompt, sanitized prompt (auto redacted), tokenized view (tokens with position). Click a token to highlight related model attention or cache usage (if available).
  - Output pane: streamed partial output captured, error marker inserted at the token index where failure occurred (if model error). For timeouts, show last emitted token + ETA when timeout occurred.
  - Inline rerun toolbar: "Trim prompt", "Reduce max_tokens by 50%", "Switch to model: rdm-lite-v2", "Force CPU fallback". Each action runs a quick ephemeral trial (capped tokens/time) and returns result inline without changing production routing. Results are annotated with delta in latency and success/failure.

- Right column: Correlated signals and provenance
  - Recent commits / model rollouts that touched the model binary/version pinned to requests (link to GH PRs).
  - Host-level metrics snapshot for the instance that served the request (GPU utilization, memory, oom events).
  - Traces (link to trace view) and logs filtered to the trace id.
  - Similar-failures graph: list of recent requests with matching fingerprints (grouping), with ability to bulk-select and mark as incident / ignore / investigate.

Wireframe annotations and interaction patterns (draft):
- Error pill colors: orange = degraded (5xx transient), red = hard model failure (invalid output)/OOM/timeouts > SLO.
- Keyboard shortcuts: G then F -> open Failure Investigator for selected request; R -> quick rerun; H -> open hypothesis notes panel.
- Ephemeral trials: must run in controlled sandbox; show billing/compute cost estimate inline (< $0.01 typical).
- When a rerun fixes the issue, prompt an optional quick survey: "Did that fix your problem? (yes/no)" to help tune suggested actions.

Decision tree for automated suggestion engine (sketch):
1) If latency >= configured timeout threshold -> suggest "rerun with increased timeout" and "switch to lower-latency model".
2) If logs contain OOM or device reset -> suggest "route to dedicated pool" and tag as infra.
3) If output parse error (invalid JSON) -> suggest "auto-sanitize prompt" and show offending span + example corrected prompt.
4) If cache_miss ratio high for this route in last 10m -> suggest "warm cache / enable prefix caching".
5) If multiple similar fingerprints in N minutes -> suggest bulk actions (mark incident, bulk rerun on fallback model).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Failure Investigator screen accessible from request list and trace links.
- Fingerprint auto-tagging with at least 6 rule-patterns (timeout, oom, invalid-json, decode-error, network-reset, kv-cache-miss).
- Inline rerun implemented as a sandboxed dry-run limited to 5s/128 tokens, with results displayed inline.
- Similar-failures grouping by fingerprint with at least 1h / 24h filters.
- Basic host metrics snapshot (GPUTemp, mem%, last OOM).

Open UX questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- How intrusive should suggested primary action be? (CTA vs. suggested only)
- Ephemeral reruns could introduce load noise. Need quota and cost guardrails. Where to surface those policies?
- Fingerprinting: heuristic rules vs. ML classifier. Start heuristic, collect labels from engineers for training set.
- Data retention: to enable grouping by fingerprint we need retention of request metadata — how long is acceptable for privacy/compliance?

Backlog grooming (short-term tickets):
- [IF-1015] Implement fingerprint rule engine (spec for initial 6 rules). Assignee: Marcus. Est: 5d.
- [IF-1016] Wireframe refinement and accessibility pass. Assignee: Jasmine. Est: 3d.
- [IF-1017] Sandbox rerun API and cost estimator. Assignee: Platform eng. Est: 7d.
- [IF-1018] Store request metadata retention policy proposal (legal/product). Assignee: Leo. Est: 4d.
- [IF-1019] Similar-failures grouping UI prototype + pagination. Assignee: Frontend. Est: 6d.

Notes for engineers:
- Expose per-request route, model version, host id, trace id in the Investigate payload. Minimal required fields, keep payload small (avoid full prompt duplication by reference to stored blob).
- Rerun should default to using the same deterministic seed and environment; sandbox must mount a config that prevents external side effects and billing surprises.

Design sketches (textual):
- Compact mode (90% density): collapse input/output to single toggles and promote fingerprint/CTA. Used by fast triage.
- Expanded mode: full token alignment, side-by-side attention heatmap (future).

Example scenario walkthrough:
- Trigger: Customer reports spike in 5xx on route /chat-stream. SRE opens Failure Investigator for a sample request.
- Investigator shows fingerprint: inference-timeout (confidence 0.86). Suggested action: rerun with fallback model rdm-lite-v2. Engineer clicks "try fallback". Ephemeral run returns success in 320ms. Investigator annotates that fallback decreases latency by 45% and marks the sample request as mitigated; links to bulk action to migrate 10% of traffic to fallback model.

Next steps (this doc):
- Sync with platform to validate sandbox rerun API.
- Prototype wireframe in Figma (Jasmine) using the 3-column layout.
- Start small: implement fingerprint rules + read-only investigator that surfaces existing logs and traces.
